description: Emergency generator minimum 48-hour on-site fuel supply required at Pennsylvania licensed hospitals
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER / FUEL SUPPLY: The electrical specifications and generator design for the proposed {occupancy} do not comply with 28 Pa. Code §101.33, which requires a minimum 48-hour on-site fuel supply for essential electrical system generators at Pennsylvania-licensed hospitals. The submitted specifications indicate a fuel tank capacity of less than 48 hours at full generator load. Fuel storage must also comply with NFPA 30 for flammable and combustible liquid storage. Revise the generator fuel system design to provide the required 48-hour minimum fuel supply and resubmit for PADOH review.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the fuel consumption rate (gallons per hour) for all essential electrical system generators at full rated load; size the on-site fuel storage tanks to provide a minimum 48-hour supply at that rate and document the calculation in the electrical design narrative.
2. Show on the electrical and plumbing drawings the revised fuel storage tank configuration, secondary containment, fill/vent connections, fuel transfer pump and day-tank arrangement; specify materials and tank standards per NFPA 30 and NFPA 110.
3. Include the 48-hour fuel supply requirement and NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance statement in Division 26 electrical specifications; reference 28 Pa. Code §101.33 in the specification section.
4. Coordinate the fuel tank installation with local authority and Pennsylvania DEP underground or above-ground storage tank regulations; include tank registration requirements in the project closeout checklist.

description: Ligature-resistant fixtures, hardware, and systems required throughout all patient care areas in licensed psychiatric units
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — LIGATURE RESISTANCE (PSYCHIATRIC UNIT): The construction documents for the proposed psychiatric inpatient unit do not demonstrate compliance with 28 Pa. Code §5100 and Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) requirements, as reinforced by PADOH DAL 2019-01, requiring ligature-resistant design throughout all patient care areas of licensed psychiatric inpatient units. A comprehensive ligature risk review of all plumbing fixtures, door hardware, overhead equipment, nurse call components, ceiling systems, HVAC registers, and window hardware must be conducted, and the drawings must specify ligature-resistant products for each of these systems. The current submittal does not include a ligature-resistant design narrative or product specifications addressing these elements.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a ligature-resistant design narrative identifying all fixture and hardware categories reviewed per The Joint Commission (TJC) Ligature Risk Evaluation requirements and PADOH DAL 2019-01; include the narrative in the construction document submittal.
2. Specify ligature-resistant plumbing fixtures (water closets, lavatories, shower fixtures) and anti-ligature door hardware (lever handles with breakaway provisions, continuous-hinge doors) on the plumbing and architectural drawings; provide manufacturer product data sheets confirming ligature-resistant ratings.
3. Specify ligature-resistant nurse call pillow speakers, anti-ligature corridor dome lights, and ceiling-mounted equipment cover plates on the low-voltage drawings; confirm that no exposed attachment points or loops exist at overhead equipment.
4. Show on the reflected ceiling plan that all ceiling systems in patient care areas are solid gypsum board with anti-ligature access panels, or specify equivalent anti-ligature lay-in ceiling products tested and documented for psychiatric use; confirm that HVAC diffusers are anti-ligature rated.

description: Pre-design ICRA meeting with PADOH regional office required for Category D projects in occupied licensed facilities
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PRE-DESIGN ICRA MEETING (CATEGORY D PROJECT): The construction documents submitted for this major renovation project in the {occupancy} do not include documentation of a pre-design infection control meeting with the PADOH regional office as required by 28 Pa. Code §51.3 for Category D projects (major renovation or new construction in occupied licensed healthcare facilities). Additionally, a written Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) prepared in coordination with the facility infection preventionist must be submitted with the construction documents. These items have not been included in the current submittal. Provide documentation of the pre-design ICRA meeting and the written ICRA prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Contact the appropriate PADOH regional office to schedule and conduct a pre-design infection control meeting prior to or during the design development phase; retain and submit to PADOH the meeting summary or minutes documenting attendees, discussion items, and agreed-upon infection control strategies.
2. Prepare a written ICRA document in coordination with the facility's infection preventionist, addressing patient risk group classification, construction activity type, required ICRA class level, and specific infection control measures to be implemented.
3. Include the ICRA document as an appendix to the construction document submittal to PADOH, with the infection preventionist's signature confirming review and approval.
4. Show on the construction documents (phasing plan or demolition plan) the physical barrier locations, HVAC isolation provisions, and construction traffic routing required by the ICRA; confirm these elements are coordinated with the pre-design ICRA meeting conclusions.

description: Pennsylvania licensed ambulatory surgical facilities require minimum 250 SF clear floor area per operating room
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ASC OPERATING ROOM MINIMUM SIZE: The floor plan for the proposed ambulatory surgical facility indicates an operating room (OR) clear floor area of less than 250 SF, which does not comply with 28 Pa. Code §551.21 governing Pennsylvania-licensed ambulatory surgical facilities. The minimum clear OR floor area of 250 SF must be measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment recesses, and column projections. Provide dimensioned floor plans confirming each operating room meets or exceeds this minimum clear area.
fix_template:
1. Revise the OR floor plan to achieve a minimum 250 SF clear floor area measured from interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment alcoves, and structural columns.
2. Provide an enlarged dimensioned floor plan for each OR clearly indicating the net clear area calculation; annotate that fixed casework, scrub sink, and column projections are excluded from the net area.
3. Confirm that the revised layout accommodates the surgical table, anesthesia equipment zone, back table, mayo stand, scrub team and circulator circulation paths, and C-arm or other imaging equipment movement per FGI 2022 ambulatory care guidelines.
4. Update the room schedule on the drawings to reflect the revised OR net clear area; include a compliance matrix identifying 28 Pa. Code §551.21 compliance for each OR in the PADOH submittal.

description: Hospital pharmacy sterile compounding must comply with USP 797/800; design reviewed by both PADOH and PA Board of Pharmacy
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / STERILE COMPOUNDING COMPLIANCE: The pharmacy design drawings for the proposed {occupancy} do not demonstrate compliance with 49 Pa. Code §27.18 (Pennsylvania Board of Pharmacy regulations) and USP Chapters 797 and 800 for sterile and hazardous drug compounding areas. The submitted floor plan does not include a pressure relationship diagram for the clean room suite, HVAC design parameters confirming ISO classification of each space, or design documentation addressing USP 800 requirements for hazardous drug handling areas. Additionally, the construction documents must be coordinated with and reviewed by the Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy in addition to PADOH. Provide the required design documentation prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Provide a pressure relationship diagram for the pharmacy clean room suite showing ISO classification (ISO 5 primary engineering control, ISO 7 buffer room, ISO 8 ante room), directional airflow arrows, and differential pressure setpoints per USP 797 and USP 800.
2. Include HVAC design parameters on the mechanical drawings for each clean room space: supply air volume (ACH), HEPA filtration (final filter 99.99% efficiency), temperature (66–72°F), relative humidity (30–60%), and room pressurization requirements (positive for sterile compounding areas, negative for hazardous drug handling areas).
3. Specify that all clean room construction finishes are non-shedding, non-porous, coved at floor-wall intersections, and capable of withstanding cleaning agents per USP 797 §5; include USP 797 and USP 800 as governing standards in the pharmacy specifications.
4. Coordinate the pharmacy design review with the Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy (PABOP); submit pharmacy drawings to PABOP as required by 49 Pa. Code §27.18 and include PABOP correspondence in the PADOH submittal package.

description: Minimum MERV 14 filtration required on supply air to all ORs; HEPA required for transplant/immunocompromised areas
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — OR SUPPLY AIR FILTRATION: The mechanical design for the proposed {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with 28 Pa. Code §107.27, which requires a minimum MERV 14 rated final filter on supply air to all operating rooms in Pennsylvania-licensed hospitals, and HEPA filtration for transplant and immunocompromised patient areas. Review of the mechanical schedule indicates that the air-handling units serving operating rooms are specified with MERV 13 final filters, which does not meet the minimum Pennsylvania MERV 14 requirement. For any bone marrow transplant or immunocompromised patient care areas, HEPA filtration (99.97% at 0.3 μm) is required. Revise the mechanical design and specifications accordingly.
fix_template:
1. Revise the air-handling unit specifications and filter schedule to specify minimum MERV 14 rated final filters (per ASHRAE 52.2) on all AHUs serving operating rooms; confirm the filter housing and rack design accommodate MERV 14 thickness and face velocity.
2. For AHUs or terminal units serving bone marrow transplant units, stem cell transplant patient rooms, or immunocompromised patient care areas, revise the specifications to provide HEPA filters (99.97% at 0.3 μm per IEST-RP-CC001) as the final filter stage.
3. Verify and document on the mechanical drawings that design air change rates and supply volumes for ORs are maintained after accounting for the increased pressure drop of MERV 14/HEPA filters; provide revised static pressure and fan selection calculations.
4. Include a filter replacement and maintenance plan in the operating and maintenance manual addressing the increased frequency of MERV 14/HEPA filter monitoring and replacement; reference 28 Pa. Code §107.27 in the mechanical specifications.

description: Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code compliance required; local building permit required in addition to PADOH approval
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PENNSYLVANIA UNIFORM CONSTRUCTION CODE (UCC): The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not include a code compliance analysis referencing the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code (UCC) as enacted by Act 45 of 1999 and codified at 34 Pa. Code §403. All hospital construction in Pennsylvania must comply with the PA-adopted model building codes and Pennsylvania amendments. Additionally, a local building permit from the local building code official (municipality or third-party agency enforcing UCC) must be obtained in addition to PADOH plan review approval. Evidence of local building permit submission or issuance has not been included in this submittal. Include a PA UCC compliance statement and demonstrate that the local permit process has been initiated.
fix_template:
1. Prepare and include a Pennsylvania UCC code compliance statement on the cover sheet of the construction documents identifying the adopted model codes (IBC, IMC, IPC, NFPA 101, etc.) with PA amendments, the occupancy classification (I-2), and the construction type.
2. Confirm with the applicable local building code official (municipality or UCC-certified third-party inspector) that a local building permit application has been submitted; include the permit application receipt or permit number in the PADOH submittal when available.
3. Review and incorporate any local PA UCC amendments or local ordinances applicable to healthcare occupancies in the project municipality into the construction documents.
4. Coordinate the PADOH plan review and local UCC permit review schedules to ensure both approvals are obtained before commencing construction; note that PADOH approval does not substitute for the local UCC building permit.

description: Certificate of Need required for hospital capital expenditures exceeding $5 million or projects adding services/beds
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CERTIFICATE OF NEED (CON): The proposed project for the {occupancy} appears to involve capital expenditures exceeding $5 million and/or the addition of new inpatient beds or health services, which requires a Certificate of Need (CON) from the Pennsylvania Health Policy Board (HPB) under 28 Pa. Code §401. CON approval must be obtained prior to commencement of PADOH plan review for projects meeting these thresholds. The current submittal does not include evidence of CON approval or an HPB determination letter confirming that the project does not require CON review. Provide this documentation before PADOH plan review can proceed.
fix_template:
1. Determine whether the proposed project meets the CON threshold under 28 Pa. Code §401 by calculating total capital expenditures and identifying whether new licensed beds or services are proposed; consult with the Pennsylvania Health Policy Board if the threshold applicability is uncertain.
2. If CON is required, submit a complete CON application to the Pennsylvania Health Policy Board and obtain a CON approval letter before proceeding to PADOH plan review.
3. If the project does not require CON (e.g., capital expenditure below threshold, no new beds or services), obtain a written determination or exemption letter from the Health Policy Board and include it in the PADOH plan review submittal.
4. Include the CON approval letter or exemption determination as the first document in the PADOH construction document submittal package; PADOH cannot initiate plan review without this documentation for qualifying projects.

description: Comprehensive ICRA Class III minimum required for all construction in occupied licensed hospitals; daily inspection logs required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL (ICRA CLASS III MINIMUM): The construction documents for the proposed project affecting occupied areas of the {occupancy} do not include an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) designating at least Class III infection control measures as required by 28 Pa. Code §51.3. Pennsylvania requires comprehensive ICRA implementation for all construction activities in occupied licensed hospitals. Additionally, written daily ICRA inspection logs must be maintained throughout construction and must be available for review by PADOH surveyors at any time. Neither the ICRA document nor the daily inspection log protocol has been included in this submittal. These items are required prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Complete a comprehensive ICRA matrix with the facility's infection preventionist identifying the patient risk group and construction activity type; the minimum resulting ICRA class must be Class III for occupied licensed hospital areas.
2. Document the specific ICRA Class III measures on the construction documents: sealed construction barriers from floor to deck, HEPA-filtered negative air machines maintaining negative pressure in construction zones, dedicated construction entry/exit with tacky mats, and prohibition on opening barriers during occupied patient care hours without prior infection control approval.
3. Develop a written daily ICRA inspection log template per PADOH requirements; the log must be completed each working day by a designated competent person and be retained on-site for immediate review by PADOH surveyors.
4. Identify the facility infection preventionist responsible for ICRA compliance oversight during construction; include their name and contact information in the construction document submittal.

description: PADOH plan review submission required for licensed hospital construction with completed application, fee, and project narrative
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PADOH SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: The construction document submittal for the proposed {occupancy} is incomplete and does not meet the requirements of 28 Pa. Code §51.3 and §103. A complete PADOH construction document submission must include: a completed PADOH plan review application, the applicable plan review fee, a written project narrative describing the scope and nature of work, and a complete set of construction documents including site plan, floor plans, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection drawings, and specifications. The current submittal is missing [application / fee / narrative / required drawing disciplines]. Resubmit with all required components.
fix_template:
1. Complete the PADOH Health Care Facility Plan Review Application (available from the PADOH Division of Safety Inspection) and include it as the first document in the submittal package; ensure all facility identification, licensure, and project description fields are completed.
2. Include the applicable PADOH plan review fee calculated per the current PADOH fee schedule (based on estimated construction cost); provide a check or money order payable to 'Commonwealth of Pennsylvania' or use the PADOH electronic payment portal.
3. Prepare a written project narrative (minimum 2–3 pages) describing the scope of work, affected areas, occupancy classification, bed count impact, construction type, fire protection systems, and infection control approach; include the narrative in the submittal package.
4. Ensure the construction document package is complete per the PADOH submittal checklist: site plan, floor plans at 1/8 inch = 1 foot minimum scale, reflected ceiling plans, sections and elevations as needed, mechanical (HVAC and plumbing), electrical, fire protection plans, and project specifications; submit to the PADOH Division of Safety Inspection.
